analyst_view.overall: Crystal Palace (21st, 5 points) and Real Sociedad (20th, 5 points) are level just outside the play-off places, so both need points. Palace sacked Pierre Sage last week and Thomas Frank lost his first game 3-2 at Coventry, saying the side 'can't concede three goals'; the numbers know nothing about the change. A correction to yesterday's view: Yeremy Pino's and Jean-Philippe Mateta's bans are Premier League ones, so both can play here (Sports Mole, SoccerNews), but Adam Wharton is banned in Europe, and Ismaila Sarr, Chadi Riad and Takehiro Tomiyasu are out with Oscar Mingueza a doubt. For Sociedad, Barrenetxea and Odriozola are out, but Jon Aramburu, whom the numbers count as missing, is in the predicted line-ups, Luka Sucic is now expected to start after an earlier report of illness, and Mamadou Sarr is doubtful. Norwegian referee Rohit Saggi (about 3.8 cards a game) is counted; I keep only a small lean lower on goals and shots.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals and add 6.2% to Palace's side because Aramburu is listed missing, but Sports Mole and Flashscore both have him starting at right-back, which takes a little of that back. Palace also lose Wharton, their main passer, while Pino and Mateta are available after all, so my earlier larger cut no longer holds; I go mildly lower, to about 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners, already nudged up for Real Sociedad's recent corner count (40 in six games). With Pino and McNeil on Palace's flanks and Kubo and Guedes on Sociedad's, both sides keep their wide threat, so nothing clearly points either way and I stay at about 9.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, already lifted for both sides' recent bookings (Palace 15 in six) and trimmed a little for referee Rohit Saggi's calm record (3.8 a game). Wharton, recently sent off, is out, but this is a tense game between two sides level on points under a new Palace manager, so I stay at 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.3 shots, with Real Sociedad's very busy recent shooting (106 in six games) already adding about 19% to their side. Palace miss Wharton, who sets much of their play, which the numbers do not know, but Pino and Mateta are available, so I shade it only slightly, to about 26.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.4 shots on target, already a bit lower for Palace's quieter recent attack. With Pino, Strand Larsen and Mateta available for Palace and Sucic and Oyarzabal expected for Sociedad, the finishers are mostly there, so I drop yesterday's trim and stay at about 9.4.
